market_holds: Spot $10.30 (sealed baseline 2026-11-10 18:10 UTC). The stock is -18.5% over 20 days and -10.2% over 5 days, 3% above its 52-week low, and about 35% below its 2026-10-05 close of $16.83 (Yahoo daily bars). It has no option chain and no earnings history (de-SPAC closed 2026-07-23), so there is no implied move. One day at 20d realised vol (73.8% annualised) is 4.65%. Q3 consensus revenue is thin and inconsistent: FXEmpire has $107.98M / EPS +$0.41, another calendar has $84.9M from 5 analysts, Yahoo has EPS -$0.19 from 2. FY26 revenue averages $102M (range $8.2M-$135.8M) and was last revised around the Aug 17-20 initiations: 4-5 Buys at $17-21 targets. So consensus models roughly the $100M FDA-approval milestone as Q3 revenue, and the estimates are about 80 days old. Short interest rose from 1.70M (9/15) to 3.40M (9/30) to 4.48M (10/15), 5.6 days to cover (Nasdaq). Free float is reduced by a 180-day sponsor/PIPE lock-up running to about January 2027. Selling drivers that are in the price: the 10/12 v2 CRC data (APL sensitivity 18.2%, below the 19% threshold, so the next Abbott milestone falls to about $70M; stock -16%), and Guardant's strong Shield Q3 on 11/5 (83k tests), on which FRNM fell 7% and 3% over 11/5-11/6 on 2-3x volume. Abbott said on its 10/21 call that SimpleScreen promotion began about Sept 30 and had almost no Q3 impact, so Q3 test volume is known to be close to zero.
view: This is Freenome's first earnings release as a public company, and the quarter has almost no commercial content. Abbott only began promoting SimpleScreen CRC at the end of September. The release's numbers will be dominated by accounting for the Abbott (ex-Exact) license. The resale prospectus's Q2 note says $92.8M of deferred transaction price is 'expected to be recognized upon transfer of the exclusive commercialization license', and the license text says that license is granted 'upon approval by the FDA of a Collaboration Product'. Approval came on 2026-07-27, inside Q3. The $100M approval milestone, fully constrained until then, also becomes unconstrained and is allocated mostly to obligations that are already satisfied. My own arithmetic therefore puts Q3 GAAP revenue near $180-195M, against a consensus of $85-108M that appears to model only the milestone. GAAP EPS would likely be well above the +$0.41 high estimate, unless SPAC-related fair-value charges offset it. That is a real mismatch between the stale consensus and the likely headline, and it arrives in a stock that is oversold, under a rising short position and near its $10 SPAC reference. It favours a better-than-feared open. But the revenue is non-cash: the upfront payment was received in 2025, and the milestone cash was already expected and is already in the stated runway 'through 2028'. Five sell-side analysts and the call will say so before the open. What the stock actually trades on is the commercial line: early Abbott ordering, the Medicare rate, the v2 PMA timing and the competitive gap to a fast-scaling Shield. Momentum on all of these has been negative, and I found no fresh datapoint showing how the launch is going. Net, I see a mild upward lean and not a bet.
unpriced: The likely recognition of about $92.8M of deferred license revenue on top of the milestone in Q3, which the thin, roughly 80-day-old consensus ($85-108M Q3 revenue) does not appear to model. It is a headline surprise and not an economic one, so it is unclear whether it moves the opening print.

recommendation.reason: Disclosed ASC 606 terms point to a Q3 revenue and EPS headline far above a stale consensus, landing in an oversold stock with growing short interest. But the surprise is non-cash and will be explained on the 16:30 ET call before the scored open. The economically relevant lines (early adoption, pricing, competition against Shield) have no fresh public datapoint I could find. That keeps my probability below the 65 needed to recommend.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Weak or absent early SimpleScreen ordering data on the call (or a sub-Shield Medicare rate), which would turn the session into a confirmation of the competitive fear the stock has been trading on.

self_critique: The 'beat' is accounting, so sophisticated holders and the five covering analysts will look through it, possibly in the release itself if the company leads with a non-GAAP or cash framing. My revenue figure is my own arithmetic from the Q2 disclosure, and SPAC-related fair-value charges could swamp GAAP EPS. The stock's real driver is competitive positioning against a fast-scaling Shield, and momentum there is clearly negative; first public quarters of de-SPACs often bring an opex step-up and cautious commentary. A down open is entirely plausible, so a 57 is about as far from 50 as this evidence allows.
approach_notes: P4 ('priced in is a claim to prove') and the own-arithmetic route paid off: rebuilding Q3 revenue from the ASC 606 notes exposed a stale consensus. P6 ('find the line it trades on') kept me from treating a non-cash headline as the mechanism. The source lists in P3 had little to offer for a name with no commercial history yet.
